title: ModelSpec
description: Output of data-modeling; input to data-discovery in resolution mode. One machine-readable spec per engagement covering the full star (facts + dimensions), Kimball-style. A human review gate sits between this artifact and discovery -- see references/toolkit-conventions.md. data-modeling only sources from a verified curated silver layer; silver_verification records that check.

silver_verification.description: data-modeling is gold-layer only. It must verify a usable curated silver layer exists before proposing a model, and refuse or flag clearly otherwise.

evidence.description: Concrete signals checked: presence of declared PK/FK constraints, documented column comments/descriptions, deduplication (no raw-ingest duplicate natural keys), conformed/standardized types and naming, absence of raw ingestion artifacts (_rescued_data, ingest batch/file columns), presence of business-meaningful (not source-system) naming.

validated_against_measures.description: True only if every measure was checked to be well-defined (additive/semi-additive/non-additive, and correctly aggregable) at exactly this grain.

source_joins.description: Non-null only when this fact's source_to_target_mappings span more than one source object -- e.g. attributes living one grain level up on a header table (1:many rolled down to the fact's own grain) plus a dimension surrogate-key lookup. Same structured, equality-only shape as contracts/data-contract.schema.json's table-level source_joins (kept in sync deliberately -- data-modeling designs this join against real, silver-verified objects; data-discovery's resolution mode then validates and carries it through into the data-contract unchanged, per skills/data-discovery SKILL.md). A join that can't be expressed as an equality condition has no home here -- that's a signal this fact's design itself needs re-thinking (a genuine fan-out risk usually means the grain or the join direction is wrong), not something to route around at the pipeline layer.

driving_object.description: catalog.schema.table -- the fact's own grain-defining source object.

left_expression.description: Same free-text-SQL precedent as source_to_target_mappings[].transformation -- a bare expression, no trailing SQL comment.

join_alias.description: Which of this fact's source_joins.driving_alias or source_joins.joins[].alias source_object/source_column actually come from. Required (non-null) on every mapping when the fact declares source_joins; null/absent otherwise.

conformance_group.description: Non-null when kind is conformed: the shared identifier used across every fact/star that references this dimension, so it is built once and reused rather than redefined per star.

source_joins.description: Non-null only when this dimension's attributes come from more than one source object -- the classic 'denormalize a snowflaked dimension' case (e.g. product + product_category + product_model, category self-joined once more for a parent category). Same structured, equality-only shape as facts[].source_joins/contracts/data-contract.schema.json's table-level source_joins.

alias.description: Unique among driving_alias and every other joins[].alias -- lets a self-joined object (e.g. product_category joined once directly and once more via ParentProductCategoryID) appear twice with distinct provenance.

scd_rationale.description: Why this attribute got this SCD type -- e.g. 'type 2: business asked to track historical territory reassignment for commission recalculation' vs 'type 1: correction-only field, history not meaningful'.

join_alias.description: Which of this dimension's source_joins.driving_alias or source_joins.joins[].alias source_object/source_column actually come from. Required (non-null) when the dimension declares source_joins; null/absent otherwise.

bridge_definition.description: Non-null only when kind is bridge.

design_rationale_ref.description: Path/URI to the companion human-readable design rationale document produced alongside this machine-readable spec.
